resale_co.name: Housing Certificate of Occupancy (Resale Inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Housing Division, Department of Code Enforcement
resale_co.lead_time: Apply early: the Township FAQ says the current wait for an inspection is about 1 month because of seasonal volume
requirements: Smoke alarms tested; interconnected alarms must all sound together; smoke alarms replaced every 10 years (NFPA 72)
Smoke alarms at least 3 feet from air vents or bathrooms with a tub or shower
CO alarms near all sleeping areas in homes with fuel-burning appliances, fireplaces or attached garages
Permanent 'CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER' label within 18 inches of the main panel and meter if the home has a generator, solar panels, battery storage or other secondary power
GFCI outlets tested (bathrooms, kitchens, garages, basements, outside); defective ones replaced
Fireplace or wood stove over 3 years old needs a Level 2 (NFPA 211) safety certification before the certificate is issued
Oil or gas furnace must be inspected and certified safe by a heating professional before the certificate is issued
Bath exhaust fans working and free of lint; kitchen range hood filter clean and working
Electric power on for the inspection; an adult (18+) must be present (no lock box access)
All Building Division permits must be inspected and closed

resale_co.how_to_apply: Submit the online Resale Inspection Application (with online payment) on the Township Form Center, or contact the Housing Division at 641 Plainsboro Road, Plainsboro, NJ 08536 (609-799-0909 ext. 1214, housingdivision@plainsboronj.com). A Buyer's Acceptance Form is also available online.

resale_co.notes: Fees are from Ordinance 25-12 (adopted November 12, 2025; the Township's fee page says the revised schedules took effect 12/8/2025) and the online application. The ordinance PDF is a scan and was read visually. The ordinance and form list single family/townhouse and condominium fees only; no separate two-family fee is published. The staff email addresses are shown on the Housing Division page as mailto links. The same Housing inspection is also required for rentals, which is not a resale item.

fire_cert.notes: The state LEA registry lists Plainsboro as a municipal enforcing agency. Ordinance 25-13 (adopted November 12, 2025) makes the Division of Fire Prevention within the Department of Code Enforcement the local enforcing agency, notes that the former Plainsboro Fire District No. 1 was dissolved effective December 31, 2024, and lists no smoke/CO certificate fee. The state fire directory lists 'Plainsboro Twp Housing Dept' in its smoke detector compliance block, and the Housing Division's resale inspection tests smoke and CO alarms, so the smoke/CO check appears to be handled in the Housing resale inspection. No official page says whether a separate smoke/CO certificate or fee applies. The Housing resale guidelines do not mention a fire extinguisher.

other_items.label: Open building permits
other_items.detail: All permits with the Building Division must be inspected and closed (Building Division 609-799-0909 ext. 2545).

other_items.label: Heating and fireplace certifications
other_items.detail: A heating professional's certification for oil or gas furnaces, and a Level 2 NFPA 211 certification for fireplaces or wood stoves over 3 years old, must be received before the Housing Certificate of Occupancy is issued.

other_items.label: Buyer's Acceptance Form
other_items.detail: The Housing Division posts a Buyer's Acceptance Form online; the fee ordinance charges $150 for composing a buyer's acceptance agreement and performing a reinspection.
